questions_and_answers.question: Zeff Co. prepared the following reconciliation of its pretax financial statement income to taxable income for the year ended December 31, its first year of operations: Pretax financial income $160,000 Nontaxable interest received on municipal securities (5,000) Long-term loss accrual in excess of deductible amount 10,000 Depreciation in excess of financial statement amount (25,000) Taxable income $140,000 Zeff's tax rate for the year is 40%. In its income statement, what amount should Zeff report as income tax expense -- current portion?

Zeff Co. prepared the following reconciliation of its pretax financial statement income to taxable income for the year ended December 31, Year 1, its first year of operations: - Pretax financial income: $160,000 - Nontaxable interest received on municipal securities: ($5,000) - Long-term loss accrual in excess of deductible amount: $10,000 - Depreciation in excess of financial statement amount: ($25,000) - Taxable income: $140,000 Zeff's tax rate for Year 1 is 40%. In its Year 1 income statement, what amount should Zeff report as income tax expense—current portion? A. $52,000 B. $56,000 C. $62,000 D. $64,000
questions_and_answers.answer: In its year 1 income statement , Zeff should report $56,000 as income tax expense—current portion. The correct option is b. On a company's income statement, income tax expense is the sum that represents the taxes due based on its taxable income . Tax expenses are included, both current and future. Taxable income: $140,000 Tax rate: 40% Income tax liability = Taxable income × Tax rate Income tax liability = $140,000 × 0.40 Income tax liability = $56,000 The correct answer is b. $56,000. Learn more about taxable income at: brainly.com/question/30617249 #SPJ4
